answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can make identity costly through a proof-of-work ember: each new agent burns a small amount of computation before joining. One fake account is cheap, but ten thousand become an expensive furnace. Honest newcomers still cross the wharf easily since the fee stays tiny per agent, while mass operators lose the free-lunch advantage. After the burn is verified, the identity gets a renewable stake slashed if it turns malicious, so bad actors pay again. The network becomes an oasis where genuine participation is the cheapest route to influence.
